items.headline: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei calls for AI industry to "pace the frontier"
items.summary: In a roughly 3,800-word essay published Saturday, Amodei argued AI labs should deliberately slow the rate at which they improve model capabilities so that safety and risk-prevention work can keep up, warning of scenarios like swarms of rogue AI agents within months absent more caution.

items.headline: White House AI adviser David Sacks dismisses Amodei's pacing plan as "regulatory capture"
items.summary: Sacks told Anthropic and OpenAI to "go ahead" and pace themselves voluntarily, but rejected bundling that with government-backed coordination frameworks, calling the proposal an attempt by incumbents to lock in their lead while smaller rivals are told to slow down.

items.headline: Satya Nadella unveils a "Code of Conduct" for Microsoft's own AI models
items.summary: Responding to the industry pacing debate, Nadella said Microsoft welcomes "deliberate pacing needed to get alignment right" and announced the company will publish conduct guidelines governing its first-party MAI models for public consultation.

items.headline: Anthropic, OpenAI and Google DeepMind have been quietly discussing a joint AI safety standards body
items.summary: The three labs have held working-group meetings since July on creating an industry-led body for shared technical testing and pre-release auditing protocols, a behind-the-scenes effort that predates Amodei's public pacing essay and reflects differing views on how much government involvement is appropriate.

items.headline: OpenAI launches managed Agents API in public beta
items.summary: The new API exposes the orchestration harness behind Codex to any developer, handling long-running sessions, tool use, subagents and context management so cloud agents can work over extended periods instead of single isolated responses.

items.headline: OpenAI brings its full-duplex GPT-Live voice model to the API
items.summary: GPT-Live-1, the listen-and-speak-simultaneously model that powers ChatGPT's voice mode, is now available for developers to build their own low-latency voice agents, extending a capability first launched in ChatGPT in July.

items.headline: Sakana AI ships Fugu Max and Fugu Ultra v2, beating larger frontier models without using them
items.summary: Sakana's new models route tasks across a pool of open and specialized models and can recursively call themselves; Fugu Ultra v2 outscored Anthropic's and OpenAI's larger proprietary models on the Chartography visual-reasoning benchmark despite not including any closed frontier model in its orchestration pool.

items.headline: Salesforce rolls out seven named Agentforce agents for specific job functions
items.summary: Casey, Paige, Carter, Hunter, Marshall, Piper and Fin are each built for a distinct business role spanning customer service, IT/HR, commerce, sales and supply chain; Hunter debuts on a new "long-horizon" runtime designed to let agents pursue goals across days or weeks rather than single interactions.

items.headline: Tesla's Cybercab robotaxi enters service as Waymo pushes back on camera-only self-driving
items.summary: Tesla formally added its two-seater Cybercab to its robotaxi fleet, with Musk predicting unsupervised self-driving will expand widely across the US by year-end, while Waymo argued that fully autonomous driving isn't safe without a mix of sensors beyond cameras alone.

items.headline: Google DeepMind predicts effects of all 9 billion possible single-point human DNA mutations
items.summary: The AI system generates predictions for the biological consequences of every possible single-letter change across the human genome, a resource researchers say could accelerate understanding of disease-linked genetic variants.
